teaser.text: Apple sells devices, software and services that fit together into a single customer relationship. A dollar enters when a customer or business partner buys a product, access or a transaction, and leaves as Apple pays suppliers, workers, content providers and other operating costs before keeping the remainder.

blocks.heading: Where could Apple's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Bear probability is 25%; base is 55%. Bull probability is 20%. iPhone Duo preorders begin October 16 and availability begins October 23. Another market expansion is scheduled for October 30. Completed deliveries, cancellations and returns matter more than wait times alone. Apple promised to expand Siri AI beyond English during October; repeated use and upgrade behavior will show whether it matters. The view improves if supply constraints ease, premium upgrades hold and Services growth supports cash generation. It weakens if memory costs rise, refunds fade and demand slows. Apple’s installed base creates value only if AI and Services turn it into durable cash growth.

It is $315.38 in October 2028. The October 2029 weighted price is $313.03, also a 6% loss with dividends. The last-date range runs from $193.85 in the bear case to $453.79 in the bull case. Today’s supplied price is $336.64.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Apple?

paragraphs.text: Bear earnings fall from $133,280 million to $129,850 million, then reach $126,225 million as shortages, memory costs and weaker operating leverage erode margins. Bull earnings rise from $144,200 million to $162,400 million, then reach $181,500 million if supply improves and AI and Services lift upgrades.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Apple really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations after spending on long-term assets. Apple generated $111,482 million from operations in 2025. After capital spending, free cash flow was $98,767 million, or 23.7% of revenue. That was below the prior year despite higher earnings, so one year’s cash conversion needs explanation.

Stock compensation is not an immediate cash payment, so Apple adds it back in operating cash flow. But it gives employees claims on the business. Deducting $12,863 million of stock pay leaves “real free cash flow” of $85,904 million, or 20.6% of revenue. That is an analytical measure, not Apple’s reported one, and it should not be deducted twice.

blocks.heading: Is Apple’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: From fiscal 2021 through fiscal 2025, Apple generated $511,554 million of free cash flow and paid shareholders $513,571 million. In 2025, it generated $98,767 million but distributed $106,132 million. Buybacks accounted for $90,711 million and dividends for $15,421 million. A buyback purchases shares from sellers, reducing the number remaining; that can increase each remaining share’s claim on profits, but only if Apple does not overpay or sacrifice better investments.

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $1.10 per share to $1.14, then $1.18. That follows five years of increases and management’s stated intention to raise the dividend annually. The bear case holds each period at $1.08, while the bull case reaches $1.24 as stronger cash generation permits faster increases.

The bear case would gain support during FY2027–FY2028 if shortages delay shipments, memory costs rise and tariff refunds fade before gross margin stabilizes. It would strengthen in FY2028–FY2029 if iPhone replacement slows, AI fails to prompt upgrades or China competition persists.

blocks.heading: What is Apple’s dividend yield at the current price?

paragraphs.text: Revenue recovered in fiscal 2025 after declining in 2023, while operating margin rose across the five-year period. Computed free cash flow—as cash from operations minus capital spending—as a share of revenue fell in 2025 even as earnings increased; net debt declined from its 2022 level. Apple’s share price is $336.64. Trailing P/E is 38.6x; forward P/E is 35.0x. Free cash flow yield is 2.0%; real free cash flow yield is 1.7%.

earnings.title: Apple earnings: guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: Apple's next results are expected on November 2, 2026; guidance covers revenue, iPhone growth, gross margin and operating expenses.
earnings.opening: Apple's next results are expected on November 2, 2026. Watch Apple's completed deliveries after tariff refunds.
earnings.closing: The full memo answers how Apple's business works, how it faces rivals, how management operates and what risks it carries.

blocks.heading: What has Apple guided for the September 2026 quarter?

paragraphs.text: Management guides to revenue growth of 9–11% for the September 2026 quarter and iPhone revenue growth in the mid-teens. It forecasts gross margin of 47–48%, including about one percentage point from tariff refunds, while rising memory costs could pressure the underlying margin. Forecast operating expenses are $19.1–19.4 billion.

blocks.heading: Has Apple kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Apple’s cash plan gives equal weight to net sales and operating income. Its 2025 maximum goals were US$402 billion and US$124 billion. Apple delivered US$416.2 billion and US$133.1 billion. Those measures reward scale and operating profit, but they do not directly measure free cash flow per share.

Finally, Apple promised a more personalized Siri in 2024, acknowledged a delay in March 2025 and introduced Siri AI for developer testing on June 8, 2026. A beta is a testing release, not full delivery. Apple’s leaders are therefore on shareholders’ side only if strong returns, disciplined dilution and reliable products arrive together.

blocks.heading: What are the last eight quarters of Apple results?

paragraphs.text: For the quarter ended June 27, 2026, revenue reached $109,417 million, up about 16.4%. Growth was broad: iPhone, Mac, Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories increased, while iPad declined. Pro iPhones and Mac laptops helped drive the result, and Services continued to benefit from advertising and cloud spending.

Cash remained powerful. Operations generated $34,369 million, and free cash flow reached $31,914 million after capital spending. During the first nine months of fiscal 2026, free cash flow totalled $110,197 million, while Apple completed another $8.8 billion of US deemed-repatriation tax payments. The quarter supports genuine growth, but not the assumption that a 50.1% margin is permanent.
